title: It returned nil and err != nil is still true
summary: A typed nil in an interface, fixed at the signature instead of at every call site.

turns.user: every POST /users comes back 400. validate returns nil on the good path and we still go into err != nil

assistant.body: An interface value is a type and a value together. Storing a nil *ValidationError in an error keeps the type, so the interface itself is not nil and the check fires. The quick shape is to assign in Handle only when there is something to assign.

turns.user: hang on. i am about to wire checkQuota into Handle too. do i write those four lines every single time

assistant.body: You are right, and I am dropping that suggestion. Catching it at each call site is the wrong place. The signature is the problem: return error from the start and the nil stays a plain nil.

turns.user: there are probably more of these around. checkQuota looked the same

assistant.body: Listing the functions that hand back a concrete pointer first. checkQuota has the same shape, so only its signature drops to error. Nothing inside changes, so errors.As for *ValidationError keeps working at the call sites.
